\begin{exercise} \end{exercise}1. ch3:3-5

  1. Prove that $(S^n(R),\bar{g}_R)$ is isometric to $(S^n,R^2\bar{g})$ for each $R > 0$.

  2. Prove that $(\mathbb {H}^n(R),\bar{g}_R)$ is isometric to $(\mathbb {H}^n,R^2\bar{g})$ for each $R > 0$.

  3. We could also have defined a family of metrics on $\mathbb {R}^n$ by $\bar{g}_R = R^2\bar{g}$. Why did we not bother?

(Used on p. 185.) \end{exercise}
